apoc_text: For mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.
old_note: *For mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* Wisdom of Solomon 6:6 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the graduated-accountability-by-degree-of-credentialing: mercy soon-pardons-the-meanest; the mighty are mightily-tormented. The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream anchor of the *more tolerable for Sodom* / *more tolerable for Tyre and Tsidon (Sidon)* architecture the King names at Matt 11:22 + 11:24. The judgment is real; the degrees are real; the degree-graduation by credentialing-density is the operative-fact the wisdom-stream had named and the King now names at the apostolic-mission level. The framework's reading rules out both the inherited eternal-conscious-torment monolith and the universalism-flatten — the day-of-judgment is real with real-graduated-degrees.
new_note: *For mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:6). *But I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment, than for you.* (Matthew 11:22). Mercy soon pardons the lowly; the mighty are mightily tormented. The King says it over the towns that saw his works: more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the day of judgment than for you. The judgment is real and it has degrees. Those who were shown little answer for little; those who were shown the kingdom working in their own streets answer for that. It is not one flat torment for everyone and it is not nothing; it is weighed.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:6 — *mercy will soon pardon the meanest: but mighty men shall be mightily tormented.* More tolerable for Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 11:22): the judgment is real and weighed by what each was shown.

apoc_text: But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.
old_note: *But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* Wisdom of Solomon 6:8 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the sore-trial-upon-the-mighty: the credentialed-and-the-mighty face the sore-trial. Matt 11:23's *thou, Kfar-Nachum (Capernaum), which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell* names the operative-application: Kfar-Nachum (Capernaum) the *exalted-unto-heaven* (the King's ministry-base, the Matt 9:1 *his own city,* the home-base of the gathering-mission) is the *mighty* upon whom the sore-trial falls. The wisdom-stream had named the principle; the King at Matt 11:23 names the cities under it. The *hell* (*hadēs* / *Sheol*, the underworld-of-the-dead) is the eschatological-judgment-station, not the inherited Christian eternal-conscious-torment overlay.
new_note: *But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:8). *And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.* (Matthew 11:23). A sore trial comes upon the mighty. Capernaum was mighty in the one way that counts in this chapter: it was exalted unto heaven, the King's own city where he lived and healed and taught. The sore trial for a city like that is to be brought down to hell, the grave, the place of the dead, lower than Sodom. The hell here is the pit the city goes down into, not the endless fire the pulpit reads into the word. Sodom would have stood if it had seen what Capernaum saw.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:8 — *But a sore trial shall come upon the mighty.* Capernaum, exalted unto heaven and brought down to the grave (Matthew 11:23), is the mighty under the sore trial.

apoc_text: Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.
old_note: *Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* Wisdom of Solomon 10:7 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Sodom-judgment as enduring-monument: the smoking-waste-land, the plants-bearing-fruit-that-never-come-to-ripeness, the standing-pillar-of-salt as monument-of-an-unbelieving-soul. The framework reads the verse against Matt 11:24's *more tolerable for the land of Sodom* — Sodom is the enduring-monument the King invokes as the floor against which the Galilean-cities-of-the-credentialing are weighed. The wisdom-stream had named Sodom as the abiding-witness-to-judgment; the King at Matt 11:24 deploys the architecture to locate the cities-that-saw-the-credential at the sharper-judgment-end of the graduated-accountability-scale.
new_note: *Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* (Wisdom of Solomon 10:7). *But I say unto you, That it shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment, than for thee.* (Matthew 11:24). The waste land still smoking, the fruit that never ripens, the pillar of salt standing as a monument of an unbelieving soul: Sodom was still preaching in Solomon's day. The King uses that monument as the floor. If the works done in Capernaum had been done in Sodom, Sodom would still be standing, and so it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom in the day of judgment than for the town that saw the kingdom at work in its own streets and did not turn. The smoking land is the witness against the unbelieving soul; the city with the mighty works has a sharper witness against it.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 10:7 — *a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.* Sodom, the standing monument of unbelief, is the floor the King measures Capernaum against (Matthew 11:24).

apoc_text: The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).
old_note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:18 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the greatness-through-humility architecture: the greater-one humbles himself; favour comes through the humbling. The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream Tanakh-anchor of Matt 11:25's revelation-economy logic: the Father reveals to the babes because the babes hold the disposition the wisdom-stream had named — humility before Yahuah (God). The system's wise-and-prudent operate the inverse — credential-elevation rather than self-humbling — and the revelation-channel does not reach them. The wisdom-stream named the principle; the King at Matt 11:25 names the operative-fact.
new_note: *The greater you are, the more humble thyself, and you shall find favour before Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:18). *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25). Sirach says favour before Yahuah (God) runs toward the one who humbles himself, and the greater he is, the lower he should go. Yahusha (Jesus) thanks the Father for the same thing working: these things hidden from the wise and prudent and revealed unto babes. The wise and prudent are the ones who did not humble themselves, who came to the Father with their standing in hand, and the revelation went past them to the ones with nothing to defend. Sirach names the principle; the prayer in Matthew 11 shows it happening.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:18 — *The greater you are, the more humble thyself.* Revealed unto babes, hidden from the wise and prudent (Matthew 11:25).

apoc_text: Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed to the meek.
old_note: *Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed to the meek.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:19 names THE direct verbal-anchor for Matt 11:25 at the extras-tier: *mysteries are revealed to the meek* — the precise inverse-pair the King names at Matt 11:25 (*hid from the wise and prudent, revealed unto babes*). The wisdom-stream had named the architecture at one of its strongest direct verbal-formulations; the King at Matt 11:25 prays the same architecture into his disciples' hearing. The *meek* of Sirach 3:19 and the *babes* (*nēpioi*) of Matt 11:25 are the same body: the *poor in spirit* of Matt 5:3, the *anawim*-disposition that has nothing to defend against the Father's-call. The wisdom-stream and the King name one diagnostic at one register.
new_note: *Many are in high place, and of renown: but mysteries are revealed to the meek.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:19). *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25). Sirach says it as plainly as it can be said: many are in high place and of renown, but mysteries are revealed to the meek. Yahusha (Jesus) prays the same pairing to the Father, hidden from the wise and prudent, revealed unto babes. The meek in Sirach and the babes in Matthew are the same people, the ones with nothing to defend when the Father speaks, and the high and renowned are the same people as the wise and prudent, the ones whose standing fills the space where the hearing would be. The two verses line up in their shape, high against low, hidden against revealed, and they name one rule of how Yahuah (God) gives understanding.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:19 — *mysteries are revealed to the meek.* Hid from the wise and prudent, revealed unto babes (Matthew 11:25).

apoc_text: Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.
old_note: *Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* Wisdom of Solomon 7:7 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the prayer-as-the-channel-of-the-Spirit-of-wisdom: understanding is given to the one-who-prays; the spirit-of-wisdom comes to the one-who-calls-upon-Yahuah (God). Matt 11:25-27's Father-Son revelation-economy walks the same architecture: the Son addresses the Father (*I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth*) and the Father's sovereign-revelation flows. The wisdom-stream had named the prayer-channel for the Spirit-of-wisdom; the King at Matt 11:25-27 names the prayer-channel for the Father-Son revelation-economy substance itself.
new_note: *Wherefore I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:7). *At that time Yahusha (Jesus) answered and said, I thank thee, O Father, Yahuah (Lord) of heaven and earth, because thou hast hid these things from the wise and prudent, and hast revealed them unto babes.* (Matthew 11:25). Solomon prayed, and understanding was given him; he called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came. The King thanks the Father that these things were hidden from the wise and prudent and revealed unto babes. The two agree on where understanding comes from: it is given, and it comes to the one who asks rather than the one who assumes he already has it. The babes receive what the wise cannot reach because the babes asked and the wise did not think they needed to.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:7 — *I prayed, and understanding was given me: I called upon Yahuah (God), and the spirit of wisdom came to me.* Understanding is given to the one who prays; the Father reveals to babes what the wise cannot reach (Matthew 11:25).

apoc_text: Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.
old_note: *Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 51:23 names the wisdom-stream's direct *come-unto-me* invitation-substance: draw-near, you-unlearned, dwell-in-the-house-of-learning. Matt 11:28's *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden* walks the same invitation-substance at the kingdom-King's register. The wisdom-stream wisdom-figure's invitation to the unlearned is the typological-anchor of the King's invitation to the labour-and-heavy-laden — the same body (those-bearing-the-Pharisaic-oral-tradition-burden of Matt 23:4's *they bind heavy burdens and grievous to be borne*) the King now invites to come.
new_note: *Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:23). *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28). Sirach ends his book with an invitation: draw near, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning. Yahusha (Jesus) issues the same one, come unto me, all you that labour and are heavy laden. Sirach was pointing people toward Wisdom; the one who speaks in Matthew is the Wisdom who stood beside the Maker before the world was (Ecclesiasticus 24:9; Proverbs 8:22–30), now speaking in his own voice. The load his hearers carried was the burden the scribes bound on them, *heavy burdens and grievous to be borne* (Matthew 23:4), not the Torah itself. The rest he offers is in the house of learning, not outside it.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 51:23 — *Draw near to me, you unlearned, and dwell in the house of learning.* Sirach's closing invitation is the one Yahusha (Jesus) gives at Matthew 11:28; come near, and find the rest in the house of learning.

apoc_text: Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find.
old_note: *Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 51:26 names THE strongest extras-tier verbal-anchor in the entire Hebrew library for Matt 11:29's *take my yoke upon you, and learn of me.* The wisdom-stream's wisdom-figure issues the same yoke-invitation Yahusha (Jesus) issues at Matt 11:29: put-your-neck-under-the-yoke, let-your-soul-receive-instruction. The framework's reading of Matt 11:29 as exchange-the-Pharisaic-burden-yoke-for-the-King's-rest-yoke (NOT yoke-vs-no-yoke) is anchored at the wisdom-stream-register here. The wisdom-figure of Sirach 51 had named the come-unto-me / put-your-neck-under-the-yoke / receive-instruction architecture; the King at Matt 11:29 walks the same architecture as the Word-made-flesh issuing the invitation in person.
new_note: *Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction: she is hard at hand to find.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:26). *Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.* (Matthew 11:29). Sirach's yoke is instruction, and he tells the soul to receive it, so the rest he found was not rest from the yoke but rest under it. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same thing in the same order: take my yoke, learn of me, and you will find rest for your souls. He is quoting Jeremiah, *ask for the old paths, where is the good way, and walk therein, and ye shall find rest for your souls* (Jeremiah 6:16). His yoke is not the absence of a yoke; it is the old path, his Father's commandments as he teaches and walks them, set in place of the heavy burdens the scribes had bound on men's shoulders (Matthew 23:4). Sirach put his neck under it and called it rest.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 51:26 — *Put your neck under the yoke, and let your soul receive instruction.* The yoke is the instruction and the rest is found under it, not away from it; Matthew 11:29 says take my yoke, learn of me.

apoc_text: Behold with your eyes, how that I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.
old_note: *Behold with your eyes, how that I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 51:27 names THE direct verbal-anchor for Matt 11:30's *for my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.* The wisdom-stream's wisdom-figure names the operative-fact: little-labour, much-rest under the yoke-of-wisdom. Matt 11:30's easy-yoke / light-burden walks the identical wisdom-stream architecture. The framework reads the verse-pair (Sirach 51:26-27 + Matt 11:29-30) as one architecture across the two registers: the wisdom-stream wisdom-yoke and the King's heart-Torah-yoke are the same yoke-substance, and the rest-promised under both is the rest-of-walking-in-the-good-way the prophet at Jeremiah 6:16 had named.
new_note: *Behold with your eyes, how that I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.* (Ecclesiasticus 51:27). *For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.* (Matthew 11:30). Sirach is not theorizing; he points to his own life and says look, little labour, much rest, and his neck is still under the yoke when he says it. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same of his yoke: easy, and the burden light. Neither man is describing a life without commandments. Moses said the commandment *is not hidden from thee, neither is it far off* (Deuteronomy 30:11), and John says *his commandments are not grievous* (1 John 5:3). The heavy thing was never the Torah; it was what men added to it, and the one who gave it carries it lightly.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 51:27 — *I have but little labour, and have gotten to me much rest.* Sirach's little labour and much rest under the yoke is Matthew 11:30, my yoke is easy and my burden is light.

apoc_text: For at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.
old_note: *For at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 6:28 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-yoke-leading-to-rest-and-joy architecture in the second Sirach yoke-passage (Sirach 6:24-31): the yoke-of-wisdom looks like fetters and chains initially (vv.24-25), but at-the-last yields rest-turned-to-joy. The framework reads the verse against Matt 11:29's *ye shall find rest unto your souls* — the rest-substance the King promises is the rest-substance the wisdom-stream had named at Sirach 6:28, and the journey from yoke-acceptance to rest-found walks the same shape: acceptance, instruction, the substance at-the-last yielding rest-turned-to-joy. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture twice (Sirach 6:24-31 + 51:23-27); the King at Matt 11:29 walks both witnesses simultaneously.
new_note: *For at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.* (Ecclesiasticus 6:28). *Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls.* (Matthew 11:29). Sirach's sixth chapter is about putting the neck under wisdom's yoke; her fetters look like bondage at first, and at the last you find her rest, and the rest is turned to joy. Yahusha (Jesus) offers his yoke in the same words: take it, learn of me, and ye shall find rest unto your souls. The yoke is not the opposite of the rest; it is the road to it, in Sirach and in the Messiah alike. Whoever thinks the gospel offers rest without a yoke has not read either verse, and whoever thinks the yoke is the Torah as a burden has missed that the rest is found at the end of wearing it.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 6:28 — *at the last you shall find her rest, and that shall be turned to your joy.* The rest found under the yoke at Matthew 11:29.

apoc_text: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.
old_note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:19 names the wisdom-stream's third major *come-unto-me* invitation-passage (after Sirach 6 and 51): the wisdom-figure issues the universal-invitation *come to me, all you that be desirous of me.* Matt 11:28's *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden* walks the same universal-invitation-architecture at the King's register, with the labour-and-heavy-laden specifying the audience-shape the wisdom-stream's *all you that be desirous* shares. The wisdom-stream wisdom-figure issued the come-unto-me invitation three times in Sirach (chapters 6, 24, 51); the King in Matt 11:28 issues the same invitation as the Word-made-flesh.
new_note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:19). *Come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest.* (Matthew 11:28). Wisdom has been calling this way all through Ecclesiasticus, and here she says it outright: come to me, all of you who want me, and be filled. When Yahusha (Jesus) stood in Galilee and said *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden*, it was not a new voice. It was the same one, the Wisdom who sat beside the Maker in Ecclesiasticus 24, now speaking in flesh, and the ones he calls are the ones Sirach's Wisdom had already called, the weary who want her and have not yet been fed.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* The same call Yahusha (Jesus) gives at Matthew 11:28, *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden*; Wisdom speaking before she came in flesh.

apoc_text: At that time therefore they decreed, saying, Whoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brothers that were murdered in the secret places.
old_note: *Then said they every one to his neighbour: If we all do as our brethren have done, and fight not for our lives and laws against the heathen, they will now quickly root us out of the earth. At that time therefore they decreed, saying, Whosoever shall come to make battle with us on the Shabbat day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brethren that were murdered in the secret places.* 1 Maccabees 2:41 names the Maccabean Shabbat-defense decision — the wisdom-stream's direct documentation that life-saving-overrides-Shabbat-restriction was the operative-principle in the Second-Temple period. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:11-12: the King's *kal vachomer* argument (sheep-rescue-on-Shabbat is permitted in the Pharisaic tradition; how much more a man?) walks the same architecture the Hasmonean decision had locked under threat of extinction. The wisdom-stream had named the principle; the King at Matt 12:12 names the operative-substance: the Shabbat is FOR life and rest and doing-well, not for the fence-architecture that obstructs the same.
new_note: *At that time therefore they decreed, saying, Whoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him; neither will we die all, as our brothers that were murdered in the secret places.* (1 Maccabees 2:41). *How much then is a man better than a sheep? Wherefore it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days.* (Matthew 12:12). After a thousand of their brothers were slaughtered in the caves rather than lift a hand on the sabbath, Mattathias and his men decreed that they would fight whoever came against them on that day. They were not setting the sabbath aside; they were refusing to let the heathen use the sabbath to root the people who kept it out of the earth. Yahusha (Jesus) makes the same judgment when he asks whether a man is worth more than a sheep pulled from a pit on the sabbath and answers that it is lawful to do well on the sabbath days. The sabbath was given for life; to preserve life on it is to keep it, not to break it.
member_note: 1 Maccabees 2:41 — *Whoever shall come to make battle with us on the sabbath day, we will fight against him.* Preserving life on the sabbath is doing well on it (Matthew 12:12).

apoc_text: He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.
old_note: *He that keepeth the law bringeth offerings enough: he that taketh heed to the commandment offereth a peace offering.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 35:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the mercy-substance-IS-the-true-sacrifice architecture: the keeping-of-the-law brings offerings enough; the heeding-of-the-commandment offers the peace offering. The framework reads the verse as the wisdom-stream restatement of Hosea 6:6's *I desired mercy, and not sacrifice; and the knowledge of Elohim (God) more than burnt offerings* — the same architecture Yahusha (Jesus) cites at Matt 12:7 (the second Hosea 6:6 citation in Matthew, after Matt 9:13). The Pharisaic-counterfeit-righteousness fails at the same diagnostic the wisdom-stream had named: external-credential-architecture without internal-mercy-substance is not the offering Yahuah (God) desires.
new_note: *He that keepeth the law brings offerings enough: he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:1). *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* (Matthew 12:7). Sirach says keeping the law is bringing offerings enough, and heeding the commandment is itself a peace offering. Yahusha (Jesus) quotes Hosea, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, against men who condemned the guiltless for picking grain on the Sabbath. Nothing in either verse loosens the Sabbath or the altar. What both say is that the man who holds the form of the commandment while condemning the hungry has not kept the commandment at all, and his sacrifice counts for nothing, while the one who shows mercy has brought the offering.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 35:1 — *he that takes heed to the commandment offers a peace offering.* Heeding the commandment is the offering; mercy over sacrifice at Matthew 12:7.

apoc_text: He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.
old_note: *If a man offereth a sacrifice of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous, and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 34:18 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the heart-substance-required-for-the-sacrifice-to-be-accepted architecture: a sacrifice without the heart-substance is rejected. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:7's *if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless* — the Pharisees who condemned the disciples for the Shabbat-plucking operated the credential-without-substance pattern Sirach 34:18 had diagnosed: the credentialing-form (Shabbat-fence-adherence) without the mercy-substance is the rejected-offering at the wisdom-stream register.
new_note: *He that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, his offering is ridiculous; and the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.* (Ecclesiasticus 34:18). *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* (Matthew 12:7). Sirach says the offering of a thing wrongfully gotten is laughable before Yahuah (God), and the gifts of unjust men are not received. Yahusha (Jesus) told the Pharisees that if they had understood I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, they would not have condemned his hungry disciples for plucking grain on the Sabbath. Both lines say the same thing about the altar: it does not wash the hands that bring to it. A sacrifice offered while mercy is withheld from the guiltless is the unjust man's gift, and Yahuah (God) does not take it.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 34:18 — *the gifts of unjust men are not accepted.* Sacrifice while condemning the guiltless (Matthew 12:7) is the gift Yahuah (God) does not take.

apoc_text: Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.
old_note: *For alms doth deliver from death, and shall not suffer thee to come into darkness.* Tobit 4:10 names THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the mercy-as-substance-with-eternal-weight architecture: alms (the operative-form of the mercy-substance) deliver from death. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:7's deployment of Hosea 6:6 in the Shabbat-controversy: the mercy-substance is not a soft-side of the Torah; it is the operative-substance with eternal-weight the wisdom-stream had named explicitly. The King at Matt 12:7 names the same operative-substance the wisdom-stream had named — and the Pharisaic-condemnation of the disciples reveals the system's loss of the substance the wisdom-stream had preserved.
new_note: *Because that alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* (Tobit 4:10). *But if ye had known what this meaneth, I will have mercy, and not sacrifice, ye would not have condemned the guiltless.* (Matthew 12:7). Tobit gives mercy its full weight: alms deliver from death and keep a man from the darkness. Mercy is not the soft side of the Torah, something to be set aside when the rules get strict. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same to the Pharisees on the Sabbath: if you had known what Hosea meant by mercy and not sacrifice, you would not have condemned the guiltless. The system that condemned hungry disciples had lost the thing Tobit's household had kept, and the King names the loss in Hosea's own words.
member_note: Tobit 4:10 — *alms do deliver from death, and suffers not to come into darkness.* Mercy carries eternal weight; the Sabbath condemnation showed a system that had lost it (Matthew 12:7).

apoc_text: Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.
old_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the eschatological-reversal-of-the-righteous-condemned architecture: the righteous-one whom the system condemned stands at the day-of-judgment in great-boldness before those-who-afflicted-him. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:14's Pharisaic-council-to-destroy-the-King: the system's trajectory from challenging the disciples (Matt 9:11) to slandering the King (Matt 11:18-19) to plotting destruction (Matt 12:14) is the operative-form of the architecture Wisdom 5:1 had named at the eschatological-end-point register. The day-of-judgment reverses the verdict the system rendered in the present age. The King at Matt 12:14 walks toward the cross under the same architecture Wisdom 5 had named at the wisdom-stream register; the resurrection is the operative-vindication.
new_note: *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him, and made no account of his labours.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:1). *Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.* (Matthew 12:14). The council that went out to plan his destruction was the system rendering its verdict on the righteous man. It had started by faulting his disciples, moved to calling him a drunkard and a friend of sinners, and now it was planning his death. Wisdom had already written the end of that story: the one the system condemned stands in great boldness before the faces of those who condemned him. The third day was the first installment of that standing, and the day of judgment is the rest of it, when the verdict rendered in this age is reversed in front of the men who rendered it.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:1 — *Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him.* The council to destroy him (Matthew 12:14) is the verdict this age renders; the day of judgment reverses it in front of them.

apoc_text: We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour:
old_note: *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of Elohim (God), and his lot is among the saints!* Wisdom of Solomon 5:4-5 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the system's-belated-recognition-of-the-righteous-one architecture: the same system that accounted his life madness and his end without honour recognizes at the day-of-judgment that he is numbered among the children-of-Elohim (God). The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:14's council-to-destroy: the Pharisees who plot the King's destruction will at the day-of-judgment recognize the substance Wisdom 5:4-5 had named — the same architecture operates against the heart-Torah-walking kingdom-citizens of the present age, with the same eschatological-reversal awaiting.
new_note: *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour:* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:4). *Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.* (Matthew 12:14). The men who held a council to destroy him accounted his life madness; before long they will say he casts out devils by Beelzebub. Wisdom puts their own confession in their mouths at the judgment: we fools, we accounted his life madness and his end without honour. The council of Matthew 12:14 is the first step of that story, and the verse that follows in Wisdom is its last, when they see him numbered among the children of Yahuah (God). The same reversal waits for everyone the system counts a fool for walking in his commandments now.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 5:4 — *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour.* The council to destroy him (Matthew 12:14) is the judgment of fools that the day of judgment turns into their own confession.

apoc_text: My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.
old_note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long. Make not an hungry soul sorrowful; neither provoke a man in his distress.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 4:1-2 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the bruised-reed-not-broken-and-smoking-flax-not-quenched mercy-substance: the wisdom-stream commands against making-the-needy-wait, against the hungry-soul-sorrowful, against provoking-the-man-in-distress. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:20: *a bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench.* The mercy-substance the prophet names of the King is the same substance the wisdom-stream named as the disposition required of the kingdom-citizens. The Pharisaic-system's pattern of categorical-classification-and-dismissal of the bruised and the smoking inverts both the wisdom-stream-disposition and the King's-disposition; the King restores; the system breaks-and-snuffs.
new_note: *My son, defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:1). *A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.* (Matthew 12:20). Sirach tells his son not to defraud the poor and not to make the needy eyes wait long; the next line adds not to make a hungry soul sorrowful or provoke a man in his distress. That is a description of handling the bruised reed without breaking it and the smoking flax without quenching it, which is what Isaiah said of the Messiah and what Matthew says Yahusha (Jesus) fulfilled. The disposition Sirach asks of a son is the disposition the Son carried. A system that sorts the bruised and the smoldering into categories and dismisses them has lost both the counsel and the Messiah who kept it.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 4:1 — *defraud not the poor of his living, and make not the needy eyes to wait long.* The bruised reed not broken at Matthew 12:20, asked of the son first.

apoc_text: Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.
old_note: *Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away thy face from a poor man. Turn not away thine eye from the needy, and give him none occasion to curse thee.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 4:4-5 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the kingdom-citizens' compassion-disposition: do not reject-the-supplication, do not turn-the-face-away, do not turn-the-eye-from-the-needy. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:20's bruised-reed-mercy substance: the disposition of the King walks the wisdom-stream-disposition the Pharisaic-system had abandoned through the categorical-classification-and-dismissal pattern. The wisdom-stream and the gospel name one disposition at two registers.
new_note: *Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:4). *A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.* (Matthew 12:20). Sirach is describing a face that stays turned toward the one in need, and Matthew 12:20 describes the Messiah's: a bruised reed he will not break, smoking flax he will not quench. The supplication of the afflicted is the bruised reed, and the poor man at the door is the smoking flax, easy to snap and easy to snuff. What Sirach asked of every son of Yashar'el (Israel), Yahusha (Jesus) did. A religious system that turns its face from the afflicted has abandoned the counsel and parted ways with the Messiah in the same motion.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 4:4 — *Reject not the supplication of the afflicted; neither turn away your face from a poor man.* The face the Messiah keeps toward the bruised reed at Matthew 12:20.

apoc_text: He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint.
old_note: *He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint. Do not the tears run down the widow's cheek? and is not her cry against him that causeth them to fall?* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 35:13-14 names THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the cry-of-the-bruised-heard-by-Yahuah (God) architecture: he-will-not-despise the supplication of the fatherless and the widow; the cry against the one who causes the tears reaches Yahuah (God). The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:20's bruised-reed-mercy substance: the wisdom-stream knew Yahuah (God) does not despise the bruised; the King at Matt 12:20 names the operative-disposition in his own ministry. The Pharisaic-system's plot at v.14 is precisely the act-causing-the-tears the wisdom-stream had named; the King's mercy-substance at v.20 is the operative-opposite-disposition.
new_note: *He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow, when she poureth out her complaint.* (Ecclesiasticus 35:14). *A bruised reed shall he not break, and smoking flax shall he not quench, till he send forth judgment unto victory.* (Matthew 12:20). Sirach says Yahuah (God) does not despise the fatherless when they plead or the widow when she pours out her complaint. Matthew is quoting Isaiah about the servant who will not break a bruised reed or put out a smoking wick, and he says it of Yahusha (Jesus) in the same chapter where the Pharisees are plotting to destroy him. The ones who cause the tears and the one who hears them stand side by side. The widow's cry Sirach speaks of is heard by the same one who would not break a reed already bent.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 35:14 — *He will not despise the supplication of the fatherless; nor the widow.* The bruised reed not broken (Matthew 12:20) is the same mercy toward the ones who cry.
writer_flag: Moved from 35:13 to 35:14: the old note quoted the fatherless-and-widow verse, which in the live text is 35:14, not 35:13 ('He will not accept any person against a poor man'). The old note's second sentence (the tears on the widow's cheek) is not in live 35:14 either; only 35:14 is quoted.

apoc_text: But executing your judgments upon them by little and little, you gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.
old_note: *But executing thy judgments upon them by little and little, thou gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* Wisdom of Solomon 12:10 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the architecture-of-the-hardened-disposition that-will-never-be-changed: Yahuah (God) gives place of repentance, not being ignorant of the bred-in malice and the cogitation that will never change. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:31-32's blasphemy-against-the-Ruach: the wisdom-stream knew the hardened-disposition that will never change as a possibility-of-the-heart; the King at Matt 12:31-32 names the architecture's consequence — the blasphemy of those whose cogitation has hardened against the credentialing they have seen will not be forgiven, because the disposition itself is the hardening-against-repentance the wisdom-stream had named.
new_note: *But executing your judgments upon them by little and little, you gavest them place of repentance, not being ignorant that they were a naughty generation, and that their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* (Wisdom of Solomon 12:10). *And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.* (Matthew 12:32). Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on the Canaanites little by little and gave them place of repentance, knowing all the while that their malice was bred in them and their cogitation would never be changed; the next verse calls them a cursed seed from the beginning. The King speaks of a sin that will not be forgiven in this world or the one to come, the word spoken against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) by men who had just watched the Spirit cast out devils and called it Beelzebub. Both passages describe a disposition that does not change: room to repent is given, and the heart that was never going to turn uses the room to harden. He said of such hearers that they believe not because they are not of his sheep (John 10:26).
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 12:10 — *their malice was bred in them, and that their cogitation would never be changed.* The cogitation that would never be changed is the heart behind the word against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) that is not forgiven (Matthew 12:32).

apoc_text: The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.
old_note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 27:6 names THE strongest wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for Matt 12:33-35's tree-known-by-its-fruit / out-of-the-abundance-of-the-heart-the-mouth-speaketh architecture: the fruit-declares-the-tree's-dressing; the utterance-declares-the-heart's-conceit. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture in precisely the substance the King walks at Matt 12:33-35. *O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh* (Matt 12:34) names the same diagnostic Sirach 27:6 had named: words-are-fruit-of-the-heart; bad-fruit-reveals-bad-heart-substance.
new_note: *The fruit declareth if the tree have been dressed; so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:6). *O generation of vipers, how can ye, being evil, speak good things? for out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.* (Matthew 12:34). Sirach puts the two halves side by side: the fruit shows how the tree was kept, and what a man says shows the conceit of his heart. Yahusha (Jesus) says the same two things in one breath to the Pharisees, that a tree is known by its fruit and that the mouth speaks out of the abundance of the heart. Words are fruit. Bad fruit means a bad tree, and bad speech means a bad heart, and no amount of religious credential changes what the mouth gives away.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 27:6 — *so is the utterance of a conceit in the heart of man.* Words as the fruit of the heart; *out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh* (Matthew 12:34).

apoc_text: Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.
old_note: *Praise no man before thou hearest him speak; for this is the trial of men.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 27:7 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of speech-as-the-trial-of-men architecture: hear-the-man-speak-first-because-this-is-the-trial. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:36's *every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment* — the day-of-judgment is the cosmic-version of the wisdom-stream's speech-as-trial architecture: the words-spoken are the evidence-of-the-heart-substance the judgment will weigh.
new_note: *Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.* (Ecclesiasticus 27:7). *But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.* (Matthew 12:36). Sirach says a man is tried when he speaks, so hear him before you praise him. Yahusha (Jesus) carries the same trial all the way to the end: every idle word men speak will be given account of in the day of judgment. What Sirach says a wise listener does now, the Judge will do then. The words are the evidence of the heart, and the heart is what the judgment weighs.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 27:7 — *Praise no man before you hear him speak; for this is the trial of men.* Speech as the trial of a man; at Matthew 12:36 that trial reaches the day of judgment, where *every idle word* is given account of.

apoc_text: Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.
old_note: *Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the no-word-goes-for-nought-and-the-mouth-that-belieth-slays-the-soul architecture: words have eternal-weight at the wisdom-stream register; the lying mouth slays the soul. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:36's *every idle word ... give account thereof in the day of judgment*: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture the King names at the day-of-judgment register. *By thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned* (Matt 12:37) walks the same architecture: words-as-evidence-of-the-heart-substance the day-of-judgment will weigh.
new_note: *Therefore beware of murmuring, which is unprofitable; and refrain your tongue from backbiting: for there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought: and the mouth that belieth slayeth the soul.* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:11). *But I say unto you, That every idle word that men shall speak, they shall give account thereof in the day of judgment.* (Matthew 12:36). Wisdom of Solomon says no word is so secret that it goes for nothing, and that a lying mouth kills the soul that owns it. Yahusha (Jesus) says every idle word will be accounted for in the day of judgment, and the next verse says what the accounting looks like: *by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned* (Matthew 12:37). Murmuring and backbiting feel like small, private sins. Both books say there is nothing private about them; the ear of jealousy hears everything, and the words are kept for the day.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 1:11 — *there is no word so secret, that shall go for nought.* No word goes for nothing; Matthew 12:36 says every idle word is accounted for in the day of judgment.

apoc_text: For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.
old_note: *For thou hast power of life and death: thou leadest to the gates of Sheol, and bringest up again.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the gates-of-Sheol-and-bring-up-again architecture: Yahuah (God) has the power of life and death; he leads to the gates of Sheol AND brings up again. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:40's *so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth* — the sign-of-Yonah's three-days-three-nights-in-the-heart-of-the-earth is the operative-application of the architecture Wisdom 16:13 had named: descent-to-Sheol-and-bring-up-again. The wisdom-stream knew Yahuah (God) brings up from Sheol; the King's resurrection is the credentialing-event the typology pre-announces.
new_note: *For you have power of life and death: you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). *For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.* (Matthew 12:40). The Father holds both doors: he leads down to the gates of hell and he brings up again. Yahusha (Jesus) gave that generation one sign, the sign of Jonah — three days and three nights in the heart of the earth, and then up. The resurrection was not a new idea arriving in Galilee; the library already knew that the one who has power of life and death brings up from the grave, and the King walked that road in his own body so the sign would stand in front of everyone.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:13 — *you leadest to the gates of hell, and bringest up again.* The sign of Jonah walks that road: three days and three nights in the heart of the earth, then up (Matthew 12:40).

apoc_text: O you Adam, what have you done? for though it was you that sinned, you are not fallen alone, but we all that come of you.
old_note: *O Adam, what hast thou done? for though it was thou that sinned, thou art not fallen alone, but we all that come of thee. For what doth this also profit, that we should now be promised an immortal time, whereas we have done the works that bring death?* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 7:48 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Adam-introduced-the-evil-heart-and-the-children-inherit-it architecture: Adam's sin is not Adam's alone; the children-of-Adam inherit the operative-pattern. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:43-45's empty-house parable: the cleansed-house empty-of-the-new-heart is precisely the architecture 2 Esdras 7:48 had named — the children-of-Adam without the new-heart-cleansing carry the inherited-pattern that produces the empty-house-vulnerability. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture of the inherited-evil-heart; the King's empty-house parable names the architecture's operative-form at the deliverance-without-internal-replacement register.
new_note: *O you Adam, what have you done? for though it was you that sinned, you are not fallen alone, but we all that come of you.* (2 Esdras 7:48). *Then goeth he, and taketh with himself seven other spirits more wicked than himself, and they enter in and dwell there: and the last state of that man is worse than the first. Even so shall it be also unto this wicked generation.* (Matthew 12:45). Ezra cries out to Adam that his fall did not stay with him; everyone who comes of him fell with him, carrying the grain of evil seed sown in Adam's heart from the beginning (2 Esdras 4:30). Yahusha (Jesus) describes a house swept clean of its unclean spirit but left empty, so that the spirit returns with seven worse and the last state is worse than the first. A son of Adam cleaned out but not given a new heart is that empty house; the inherited pattern comes back to fill what was only swept. The remedy is not a cleaner house but a different heart in it (Ezekiel 36:26).
member_note: 2 Esdras 7:48 — *though it was you that sinned, you are not fallen alone, but we all that come of you.* The swept but empty house of Matthew 12:45 is a son of Adam without a new heart.

apoc_text: He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).

The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:50's *whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother* — the kingdom-family-recognition-criterion is the same doing-the-Father's-will substance the wisdom-stream had named as the operative-form of the child-of-Yahuah (the Lord) identity. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture; the King at Matt 12:50 names the kingdom-family substance.
new_note: *He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:13). *For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.* (Matthew 12:50). The righteous one in Wisdom of Solomon calls himself the child of Yahuah (God), and two verses later the ungodly say why they believe him enough to hate him: his life is not like other men's, his ways are of another fashion. Yahusha (Jesus) names the family of the Father the same way, whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother, sister, mother. The child of Yahuah (God) is known by a life that does the Father's will; that is how the Father's children are recognised. The ungodly recognised it too, and it was the recognising that made them lie in wait.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:13 — *He professeth to have the knowledge of Yahuah (God): and he calls himself the child of Yahuah (God).* The child of Yahuah (God) is known by a life of another fashion; Matthew 12:50 says the same, whoever does the will of my Father.

apoc_text: For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.
old_note: *For if the just man be the son of Elohim (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the son-of-Elohim-tested-by-deliverance architecture: the just-man's son-of-Elohim-identity is to be tested by whether Yahuah (God) helps him. The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:50's kingdom-family-recognition-criterion: the doing-the-Father's-will substance is the operative-identity-marker — the system's test (Wisdom 2:18) is whether Yahuah (God) delivers; the King's test (Matt 12:50) is whether the heart walks the will of the Father. The same architecture from both sides: the heart-Torah-walking-life IS the son-of-Elohim-identity-marker at both registers.
new_note: *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him, and deliver him from the hand of his enemies.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:18). *For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.* (Matthew 12:50). The ungodly have a test for who is the son of Yahuah (God): will the Father step in and deliver him? Yahusha (Jesus) gives the Father's own test for who belongs to his family: whoever does the will of my Father in heaven. One measures sonship by rescue, the other by obedience. Wisdom shows the just man already living by the second standard before the first is ever applied to him, and that is exactly why his life was grievous to them.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:18 — *For if the just man be the son of Yahuah (God), he will help him.* The ungodly test sonship by rescue; Yahusha (Jesus) marks his family by doing the Father's will (Matthew 12:50).
