The framework reads the verse against Matt 12:50: the kingdom-family-recognition-criterion is the same doing-the-Father's-will substance the wisdom-stream had named as the operative-form of the son-of-the-Most-High identity. The wisdom-stream and the gospel name one architecture across two registers — the kingdom-family is identified by the heart-Torah-walking-disposition the wisdom-stream had named, the kingdom-entry-criterion at Matt 7:21 had named, and the 1 John 2:3-4 master-filter restates.
new_note: *Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother: so shall you be as the son of the Most High, and he shall love you more than your mother does.* (Ecclesiasticus 4:10). *For whosoever shall do the will of my Father which is in heaven, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.* (Matthew 12:50). Sirach says the man who fathers the fatherless and stands in for the widow's husband shall be as the son of the Most High, loved by him more than a mother loves. Yahusha (Jesus) says whoever does the will of his Father is his brother, sister, and mother. In both, the family of Elohim (God) is known by the doing of the Father's will, which in Sirach's example is the Torah's own care for the orphan and widow. The doing does not manufacture the sonship; it shows it, the way a son is known by bearing his father's likeness, and that is why Yahusha (Jesus) names his kin by it.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 4:10 — *Be as a father to the fatherless, and instead of an husband to their mother.* The doing of the Father's will by which the family is known at Matthew 12:50.
writer_flag: Theology adjustment: the old note read the doing as what 'makes' the doer a son of the Most High; rewritten so the doing reveals the family rather than creates it (hearing/doing reveals what was already true).

apoc_text: And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber,
old_note: *And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber, And shall be sought of many, and yet not be found: then shall unrighteousness and incontinency be multiplied upon earth.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 5:9-10 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-and-understanding-withdrawing-into-the-secret-chamber architecture: in the latter-days the understanding withdraws-itself and shall-be-sought-of-many-and-not-be-found. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:11-17's cause-and-effect-of-hearing diagnostic: the understanding the multitudes seek-from-the-parables withdraws from the system-rejecting-disposition; the wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-withdrawal-from-the-disposition-that-rejects. The disciples-receive the mysteries-of-the-kingdom because the disposition-to-receive operates; the system-rejecting-disposition encounters the withdrawn-understanding.
new_note: *And salt waters shall be found in the sweet, and all friends shall destroy one another; then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber, And shall be sought of many, and yet not be found: then shall unrighteousness and incontinency be multiplied upon earth.* (2 Esdras 5:9–10). *He answered and said unto them, Because it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given.* (Matthew 13:11). Esdras is shown a day when understanding withdraws into its secret chamber and is sought by many and not found. The King tells his disciples why he speaks in parables: to you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom, to them it is not given. Understanding does not vanish from the earth; it withdraws from those who would not have it and is given to those who hear. The many who seek and do not find in Esdras are the ones who, in Matthew, hear and do not understand, because what is withdrawn from one is a gift to the other, and the hearing reveals which is which.
member_note: 2 Esdras 5:9 — *then shall wit hide itself, and understanding withdraw itself into his secret chamber.* To some it is given to know the mysteries; to others it is not (Matthew 13:11).

apoc_text: For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject to sin.
old_note: *For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject unto sin.* Wisdom of Solomon 1:4 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the wisdom-shall-not-enter-into-a-malicious-soul architecture: wisdom does-not-enter the malicious-soul; the disposition determines the entry. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:13-15's Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 6:9-10 citation: the people's-heart has waxed-gross because they-have-closed-their-own-eyes; the wisdom does not enter the disposition-that-closes. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture-of-the-soul-that-refuses-wisdom; Matt 13:13-15 names the operative-form at the Pharisaic-system-rejecting-the-King register. The Father does not actively-prevent the hearing; the disposition closes itself; the wisdom encounters-the-closure.
new_note: *For into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter; nor dwell in the body that is subject to sin.* (Wisdom of Solomon 1:4). *Therefore speak I to them in parables: because they seeing see not; and hearing they hear not, neither do they understand.* (Matthew 13:13). Wisdom will not move into a soul that is set against her. Yahusha (Jesus) speaks in parables for the same reason he gives in the next lines, quoting Isaiah: *this people's heart is waxed gross, and their ears are dull of hearing, and their eyes they have closed* (Matthew 13:15). The parable did not shut them out; the closed eyes were their own doing, and wisdom does not force the door. In the same breath he tells the disciples their eyes are blessed because they see (Matthew 13:16). The teaching was one teaching; what differed was the soul it met.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 1:4 — *into a malicious soul wisdom shall not enter.* Wisdom does not enter a soul set against her; at Matthew 13:13 the parables meet eyes that have closed themselves.

apoc_text: When the great Yahuah (God) will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks to Yahuah (God) in his prayer.
old_note: *When the great Lord will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks unto the Lord in his prayer.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 39:6 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the spirit-of-understanding-poured-out-on-the-elect-scribe architecture: when-the-great-Yahuah-wills, the scribe shall-be-filled-with-the-spirit-of-understanding. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:16-17's *blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.* The disciples' blessing-of-seeing-and-hearing operates in the same architecture the wisdom-stream had named — the spirit-of-understanding poured-out by Yahuah (the Lord) on the elect-disciples. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture; Matt 13:16-17 names the operative-blessing at the apostolic-circle.
new_note: *When the great Yahuah (God) will, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences, and give thanks to Yahuah (God) in his prayer.* (Ecclesiasticus 39:6). *But blessed are your eyes, for they see: and your ears, for they hear.* (Matthew 13:16). Sirach says the scribe is filled with the spirit of understanding when the great Yahuah (God) wills it; the man does not work it up out of his own study, he is filled. Yahusha (Jesus) tells the disciples their eyes and ears are blessed, and the verse before explains why: *it is given unto you to know the mysteries of the kingdom* (Matthew 13:11). The seeing and the hearing are given the same way the scribe's understanding is given. The hand that fills the scribe is the hand that opens the disciple's eyes, and both of them answer with thanks.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 39:6 — *he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding: he shall pour out wise sentences.* Understanding is given when Yahuah (God) wills; the blessed eyes and ears of Matthew 13:16 are given the same way.

apoc_text: For the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness has it brought up to this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?
old_note: *For the grain of evil seed hath been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness hath it brought up unto this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing shall come?* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 4:30 names THE direct wisdom-stream parallel to the wheat-and-tares architecture at the heart-of-Adam register: the grain-of-evil-seed has been-sown-in-the-heart-of-Adam-from-the-beginning, AND the ungodliness it has produced continues-to-grow-until-the-time-of-threshing. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:24-30's *the kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field: But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat.* The wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-evil-seed-sown-from-the-beginning AND the time-of-threshing-when-the-sorting-occurs; the King at Matt 13:24-30 names the operative-parable-form. The framework reads the architecture in continuity: the watchers' incursion at Bereshit (Genesis) 6:1-4 + the dragon's corruption-of-the-line at Bereshit 3 + the seed-of-evil-sown-from-the-beginning at 4 Ezra 4:30 + the King's tares-sown-by-the-enemy at Matt 13:24-30 = one architecture across the canon and the wisdom-stream.
new_note: *For the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, and how much ungodliness has it brought up to this time? and how much shall it yet bring forth until the time of threshing come?* (2 Esdras 4:30). *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:* (Matthew 13:24). Uriel says a grain of evil seed was sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning, that it has brought up ungodliness ever since, and that it will go on bearing until the time of threshing. Yahusha (Jesus) opens his parable with a man sowing good seed in his field, and the verses that follow tell of the enemy's seed and the harvest when the two are separated. Esdras and the King both speak of seed, of two kinds of seed in one ground, and of a threshing that ends the matter. The evil seed is not the last word in either book; the threshing is.
member_note: 2 Esdras 4:30 — *the grain of evil seed has been sown in the heart of Adam from the beginning.* The parable of the good seed sown in the field (Matthew 13:24) runs to the same threshing.

apoc_text: For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.
old_note: *For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him. Thus infirmity was made permanent; and the law also in the heart of the people with the malignity of the root; so that the good departed away, and the evil abode still.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 3:21-22 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wicked-heart-inherited-from-Adam architecture: the first-Adam bore the wicked-heart; all-who-are-born-of-him inherit the operative-pattern. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:25's *while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares.* The wisdom-stream had named the inherited-wicked-heart as the architecture-the-tares-grow-in; the King's parable names the operative-form of the enemy-sowing-while-the-watchful-guard-fails. The framework reads the architecture WITHOUT collapsing into the Augustinian-original-sin doctrine in its Christian-developed form: the framework preserves the actor's-disposition (the watchful-guard-fails; *while men slept*) without erasing the actor's-responsibility; the wisdom-stream knew the inherited-heart-architecture without the Christian-doctrinal-overlay.
new_note: *For the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome; and so be all they that are born of him.* (2 Esdras 3:21). *But while men slept, his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat, and went his way.* (Matthew 13:25). Esdras says the first Adam bore a wicked heart, transgressed, and was overcome, and so are all who are born of him. The parable says that while men slept an enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat. These are two different facts about one field. The sons of Adam carry the wicked heart, and the law was given to bring fruit out of them in spite of it; the tares are another seed, planted by an enemy, not born of Adam at all. The wheat is wounded, the tares are not wheat, and the harvest will tell them apart.
member_note: 2 Esdras 3:21 — *the first Adam bearing a wicked heart transgressed, and was overcome.* The field of Adam's sons is where the enemy sowed tares while men slept (Matthew 13:25).
writer_flag: Kept the old note's line between the wicked heart inherited by Adam's sons (the wheat) and the tares the enemy sowed (a different seed); wrote it plainly so the two are not collapsed.

apoc_text: O Yahuah (God), if you suffer not your servant, that we may pray before you, and you give us seed to our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it; how shall each man live that is corrupt, who bears the place of a man?
old_note: *O Yahuah (Lord) that bearest rule, of every spirit that liveth, give us seed unto our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it; whereby every one shall live that is corrupt, who beareth the place of a man.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 8:6 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the prayer-for-seed-unto-the-heart architecture: Yahuah (Lord) is asked-for-seed-unto-the-heart and culture-to-the-understanding so-that-fruit-may-come. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:24's *the kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field.* The wisdom-stream knew the architecture of seed-given-by-Yahuah (Lord) to the heart that fruit-may-come; the King at Matt 13:24 names the operative-parable-form of the Sower-of-the-good-seed. The framework reads the architecture in continuity: the prayer of 4 Ezra 8:6 (give-us-seed-unto-our-heart) is the disposition the good-ground-soil at Matt 13:23 carries; the Sower's sowing IS the answer to the wisdom-stream's prayer.
new_note: *O Yahuah (God), if you suffer not your servant, that we may pray before you, and you give us seed to our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it; how shall each man live that is corrupt, who bears the place of a man?* (2 Esdras 8:6). *Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is likened unto a man which sowed good seed in his field:* (Matthew 13:24). Ezra prays for seed to the heart and culture to the understanding, so that fruit may come, because a corrupt man cannot live any other way. The kingdom parable answers that prayer with a sower: a man goes out and sows good seed in his field. The seed to the heart Ezra begs for is what the sower is sowing; the fruit Ezra hopes for is what the good ground brings forth (Matthew 13:23). The prayer and the parable meet in the same field.
member_note: 2 Esdras 8:6 — *give us seed to our heart, and culture to our understanding, that there may come fruit of it.* The sower of Matthew 13:24 is the answer to this prayer.

apoc_text: And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.
old_note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* Wisdom of Solomon 3:7 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the righteous-shall-shine-at-the-time-of-their-visitation architecture: the souls-of-the-righteous shall-shine and run-like-sparks-among-the-stubble at the time-of-their-visitation. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:43: the visitation-of-the-righteous at the wisdom-stream register is the same eschatological-vindication the King names at the wheat-and-tares-interpretation register. The sparks-among-the-stubble carries the harvest-and-burning imagery directly — the same harvest the King's parable names, with the righteous-shining-as-sparks-among-the-burning-tares.
new_note: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.* (Matthew 13:43). Wisdom puts the shining of the righteous at a set time — the time of their visitation — and sets it in a harvest scene: sparks running among the stubble. Yahusha (Jesus) puts it at the same moment in the parable of the tares: when the field is reaped and the tares are bundled for the fire, then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun. The stubble burning and the sparks flying are the same picture as the tares burning and the wheat shining. The shining is not yet; it waits on the harvest.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:7 — *in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* The harvest scene of Matthew 13:43 — tares to the fire, *then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun.*

apoc_text: As for wisdom, what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you: but will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not pass over the truth.
old_note: *As for wisdom, what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you; but will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not pass over the truth.* Wisdom of Solomon 6:22 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the I-will-not-hide-mysteries-from-you architecture: the wisdom-stream's teacher commits to bring-the-knowledge-into-light and not-pass-over-the-truth. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:35's *I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world*: the wisdom-stream's commitment-to-reveal-the-mysteries operates in the same register the King's parables-method enacts. The mysteries-kept-secret-from-the-foundation revealed-now to the disciples is the operative-form of the architecture the wisdom-stream had named at its teacher-register.
new_note: *As for wisdom, what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you: but will seek her out from the beginning of her nativity, and bring the knowledge of her into light, and will not pass over the truth.* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:22). *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.* (Matthew 13:35). Solomon promises to tell what wisdom is and how she came up, to hide no mysteries, to trace her from the beginning of her nativity and bring the knowledge of her into light. The King opens his mouth in parables to utter things kept secret from the foundation of the world. Both are teachers who refuse to pass over the truth; both are bringing into the light what had been hidden, and the parables, which the crowd heard as stories, were that light being given to the disciples who asked what they meant.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 6:22 — *I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you.* Things kept secret from the foundation of the world uttered in parables (Matthew 13:35) is the same refusal to hide mysteries.

apoc_text: And the men that are received shall see it, who have not tasted death from their birth: and the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into another meaning.
old_note: *And the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into another meaning. For evil shall be put out, and deceit shall be quenched. As for the faith, it shall flourish; corruption shall be overcome, and the truth, which hath been so long without fruit, shall be declared.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 6:26-28 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the truth-which-hath-been-so-long-without-fruit-shall-be-declared architecture: the latter-days will see the long-hidden-truth declared-at-last. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:35: the wisdom-stream knew the architecture-of-the-truth-revealed-after-long-hiddenness; the King's parables-method names the operative-form of the architecture the wisdom-stream had named. The truth-without-fruit-for-a-long-time = the substance-kept-secret-from-the-foundation-of-the-world; the declared-at-last = the King's-revealing-through-the-parables.
new_note: *And the men that are received shall see it, who have not tasted death from their birth: and the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into another meaning.* (2 Esdras 6:26). *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.* (Matthew 13:35). Among the tokens of the end Ezra is told that the heart of the inhabitants will be changed and turned into another meaning, and that men who have not tasted death will see it. When Yahusha (Jesus) teaches in parables he is uttering what had been kept secret from the foundation of the world, and a parable only opens to a heart that has been turned toward its meaning; to everyone else it stays a story about seed and soil. Ezra goes on to hear that the truth so long without fruit shall be declared (2 Esdras 6:28). The parables are that declaring begun, and the changed heart is the one that hears them.
member_note: 2 Esdras 6:26 — *the heart of the inhabitants shall be changed, and turned into another meaning.* The parables of Matthew 13:35 open what was kept secret to a heart turned toward their meaning.
writer_flag: The old note quoted 2 Esdras 6:26–28 and leaned on v.28 ('the truth, which hath been so long without fruit, shall be declared'), which is not in this packet. I rebuilt on the live 6:26 (the changed heart) and mentioned v.28 in prose. The author may prefer this card to sit at 6:28.

apoc_text: Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?
old_note: *Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 20:30 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-that-is-hid-and-treasure-that-is-hoarded-up architecture: the hidden-treasure has no profit-to-those-who-do-not-find-and-obtain-it. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:44's *the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field*: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the hidden-treasure-and-the-finding-and-obtaining; the King names the operative-form at the kingdom-of-heaven register. The framework's reading per the Father-Son-buyer-finds-the-treasure substance (per Red Line #11): the Father / the Son is the One-who-finds-the-hidden-treasure (the elect scattered through the field-of-the-world) and pays-the-full-price-to-obtain. The Tanakh-substance and the wisdom-stream-substance and the King's-parable-substance all carry the architecture.
new_note: *Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both?* (Ecclesiasticus 20:30). *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.* (Matthew 13:44). Sirach asks what good hidden wisdom or hoarded treasure does anyone — none, until it is found and brought out. Yahusha (Jesus) tells of treasure hidden in a field, and of the man who finds it and sells everything he has to buy the field, because treasure found is worth all of it. The man who buys the field is the one who paid the whole price: the Father, through the Son, finding his own scattered through the field of the world and giving everything to obtain them. The point Sirach made holds either way — hidden treasure profits no one until someone finds it, and finding it is worth everything.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 20:30 — *Wisdom that is hid, and treasure that is hoarded up, what profit is in them both.* The treasure hid in the field is found and bought with everything (Matthew 13:44).
writer_flag: Kept the old note's reading of the man who buys the field as the Father through the Son paying the whole price for the scattered seed hidden in the field of the world; stated plainly, not as settled. Author may want to check it.

apoc_text: A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.
old_note: *A faithful friend is a strong defence: and he that hath found such an one hath found a treasure. Nothing doth countervail a faithful friend, and his excellency is invaluable.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 6:14-15 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the finding-a-faithful-friend-is-finding-a-treasure-nothing-countervails architecture: the supreme-worth substance of the faithful-friend is incomparable; nothing equals it. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:45-46's *the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls: Who, when he had found one pearl of great price, went and sold all that he had, and bought it.* The wisdom-stream knew the architecture-of-the-finding-of-the-incomparable-worth; the King names the operative-form at the kingdom-of-heaven register. The pearl-of-great-price = the elect (per the framework's preferred Father-Son-buyer reading) AS the supreme-worth substance the buyer pays-all-to-obtain.
new_note: *A faithfull friend is a strong defence: and he that has found such an one has found a treasure.* (Ecclesiasticus 6:14). *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls:* (Matthew 13:45). Sirach says a faithful friend is a treasure, and the next verse says nothing countervails him; there is no price you could set against him. Yahusha (Jesus) says the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant seeking goodly pearls who finds one worth everything he owns and sells all to have it. Both are describing the finding of something whose worth has no equal, and both describe the finder as the one who recognized it when it was in front of him. Sirach knew that kind of worth in a friend; the Messiah says the kingdom is that kind of worth, and the one who finds it does not haggle.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 6:14 — *he that has found such an one has found a treasure.* The one pearl worth all the merchant had, Matthew 13:45.
writer_flag: Left out the old note's identification of the merchant as the Father/Son buying the elect; that reading is not in the voice skill spine I was given, so the card keeps only the incomparable-worth connection. Author may want it restored.

apoc_text: I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.
old_note: *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her. Neither compared I unto her any precious stone, because all gold in respect of her is as a little sand, and silver shall be counted as clay before her.* Wisdom of Solomon 7:8-9 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-preferred-above-sceptres-and-thrones architecture: wisdom is preferred-above-rule and esteemed-above-riches-and-precious-stones; the precious-stones are little-sand and silver-is-clay before the supreme-worth of wisdom. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:45-46's pearl-of-great-price: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-supreme-worth-preferred-above-all-else at the wisdom-register; the King names the operative-form at the kingdom-of-heaven register. The buyer (per the framework's preferred reading at short.md) is the One-who-prefers-the-pearl-above-all-else and pays-the-full-price-to-obtain.
new_note: *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:8). *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto a merchant man, seeking goodly pearls:* (Matthew 13:45). A king with a sceptre and a throne in hand says he preferred wisdom before both of them and counted riches nothing beside her. The merchant in the parable does the same arithmetic over one pearl: he sells all he has to get it. The kingdom of heaven is worth that reckoning, and the one who makes it is not throwing away sceptres and riches so much as seeing, as Solomon saw, that they were never worth what wisdom is. The pearl is found by someone already seeking goodly pearls; the finding is the moment everything else is weighed and comes up light.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:8 — *I preferred her before sceptres and thrones, and esteemed riches nothing in comparison of her.* The merchant who sells all for one pearl (Matthew 13:45) is doing Solomon's arithmetic: sceptres and riches are nothing beside wisdom.
writer_flag: Old note identified the buyer of the pearl as the Father or Son who pays all to obtain, citing an internal file (short.md). I could not verify that reading in the skill, so the rebuilt note keeps the plain comparison (king prefers wisdom / merchant sells all) and does not name who the buyer is. Author may want the buyer identification restored if it is settled teaching.

apoc_text: For she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of Yahuah (God), being commended for the gifts that come from learning.
old_note: *For she is a treasure unto men that never faileth: which they that use become the friends of Elohim (God), being commended for the gifts that come from learning.* Wisdom of Solomon 7:14 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-is-a-treasure-unto-men-that-never-faileth architecture: wisdom is the never-failing-treasure that makes-the-users-friends-of-Elohim (God). The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:44's treasure-hid-in-the-field: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-never-failing-treasure-of-wisdom; the King names the operative-form at the kingdom-of-heaven register. The treasure-hid-in-the-field is the substance-the-Father-Son-buyer-finds-and-pays-all-to-obtain (per the framework's preferred reading); the supreme-worth-of-the-treasure operates at the wisdom-stream-and-the-gospel registers together.
new_note: *For she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of Yahuah (God), being commended for the gifts that come from learning.* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:14). *Again, the kingdom of heaven is like unto treasure hid in a field; the which when a man hath found, he hideth, and for joy thereof goeth and selleth all that he hath, and buyeth that field.* (Matthew 13:44). Wisdom is a treasure to men that never fails, and those who use her become the friends of Yahuah (God). The King says the kingdom of heaven is like treasure hid in a field, found by a man who hides it again, sells all he has for joy, and buys the field. Solomon's treasure and the King's treasure are the same kind: worth everything a man owns, and the man who finds it knows it. The one who learns wisdom is commended for her gifts; the one who buys the field has the treasure and the friendship of the one who hid it there.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 7:14 — *she is a treasure to men that never fails: which they that use become the friends of Yahuah (God).* The treasure hid in a field worth selling all for (Matthew 13:44) is the treasure that never fails and makes friends of Yahuah (God).
writer_flag: Old note's buyer reading (Father or Son as the one who finds and pays all) rested on an internal reference I could not confirm in the skill; the rebuilt note leaves the buyer unnamed and keeps the treasure comparison.

apoc_text: There be many created, but few shall be saved.
old_note: *Many be created, but few shall be saved.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 8:3 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the few-shall-be-saved architecture: many-be-created-but-few-shall-be-saved. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:49's severing-the-wicked-from-among-the-just at the dragnet-recapitulation register: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-few-saved-at-the-day-of-separation; the King names the operative-form at the dragnet-of-the-net-cast-into-the-sea-gathering-of-every-kind register. The framework reads the verse in continuity with the Matt 7:13-14 narrow-gate / few-find-it architecture: the wisdom-stream knew the substance the King names; the substance is the post-harvest-sifting per Red Line #11 operative at the eschatological-end-point.
new_note: *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* (2 Esdras 8:3). *So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just,* (Matthew 13:49). Ezra is told that many are created but few saved, after the likeness of much clay and little gold (2 Esdras 8:2). Yahusha (Jesus) puts the sorting at the end of the world, when the angels sever the wicked from among the just as a net full of every kind is sorted on the shore. The net gathers all; the shore keeps few. The few saved are what remains when that severing is done.
member_note: 2 Esdras 8:3 — *There be many created, but few shall be saved.* The angels sever the wicked from among the just at Matthew 13:49; the few are what remains.

apoc_text: They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.
old_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and Yahuah (their Lord) shall reign for ever.* Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the righteous-shall-judge-the-nations and have-dominion-over-the-people architecture at the eschatological-end-point. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:49's severing-the-wicked-from-among-the-just: the wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-righteous-judging-the-nations at the eschatological-judgment-and-millennial-reign register; the King's dragnet-parable lands the architecture at the present-chapter's recapitulation register. The framework reads the kingdom-of-priests destination-of-the-gathered-remnant per Red Line #7 in continuity: the righteous judge-and-rule the nations-left-after-the-judgment at the millennial-reign; the wisdom-stream and the gospel walk one architecture.
new_note: *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Elohim (God) shall reign for ever.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:8). *So shall it be at the end of the world: the angels shall come forth, and sever the wicked from among the just,* (Matthew 13:49). Wisdom says the righteous will judge the nations and have dominion over the people. Yahusha (Jesus) says what has to happen first: at the end of the age the angels come and sever the wicked from among the just. The sorting comes before the ruling. Once the wicked are taken out from among them, the just who are left are the ones Wisdom sees judging the nations — a kingdom of priests to the peoples left alive after that day, under an Elohim (God) who reigns for ever.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 3:8 — *They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people.* After the angels sever the wicked from among the just (Matthew 13:49), the just are the ones who judge.

apoc_text: Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.
old_note: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:24 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the through-envy-of-the-devil-came-death-into-the-world architecture: the devil's envy is the source-of-death entering-the-world; they-that-hold-of-his-side find-death. The framework reads the verse against Matt 13:39's *the enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world.* The wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-devil-as-source-of-death-in-the-world; the King names the operative-form at the wheat-and-tares-interpretation register. The framework reads the architecture in continuity: the devil's envy at Bereshit (Genesis) 3 (the serpent) + the devil's seduction at the watchers (1 Enoch 6-11) + the devil's sowing-of-tares at Matt 13:39 = one architecture of the source-of-death-and-corruption across the canon and the wisdom-stream. The they-that-hold-of-his-side find-death substance is the same architecture the children-of-the-wicked-one carry: paternal-source-determines-destination.
new_note: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). *The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels.* (Matthew 13:39). Wisdom names where death came from — the envy of the devil — and who finds it: they that hold of his side. Yahusha (Jesus) names the same enemy as the one who sowed the tares in the field, and in the verse before he calls the tares the children of the wicked one. The serpent in the garden, the watchers who corrupted the earth, the sower of tares in the field — it is one enemy doing one work across the whole story. Those who are of his side come to his end, because the seed shows at the harvest.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:24 — *through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side.* The enemy who sowed the tares (Matthew 13:39) is the one whose envy let death in.

apoc_text: Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.
old_note: *Then stood up Eliyahu (Elias) the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-fiery-zeal-at-the-royal-court architecture: the prophet stood-up-as-fire and his word burned-like-a-lamp. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:3-4's *Herod had laid hold on Yochanan (John), and bound him ... For Yochanan (John) said unto him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.* Yochanan (John)'s confrontation of Herod-Antipas at the Torah-violation operates in the same Eliyahu-pattern the wisdom-stream had named at the Achav (Ahab)-confrontation register. The Matt 11:14 identification of Yochanan (John) as *Eliyahu, which was for to come* is corroborated at the prophet's-zeal-and-Torah-confrontation pattern Sirach 48 walks. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture; Matt 14 names the operative-form at the gospel-level.
new_note: *Then stood up Elias the prophet as fire, and his word burned like a lamp.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:1). *For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife.* (Matthew 14:3). Elijah's fire burned hottest at the king's court. He told Ahab to his face that the house of Ahab had forsaken the commandments of Yahuah (God), and Jezebel sought his life for it. John carried the same fire to Herod's court and said *it is not lawful for thee to have her* (Matthew 14:4), the Torah spoken against the king's own bed (Leviticus 18:16). Herod did what Ahab's house did: he laid hold on the prophet and bound him, and a queen wanted him dead. The word that burns like a lamp is not dimmed for royalty, and royalty does not forgive it.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 48:1 — *his word burned like a lamp.* Elijah's fire at Ahab's court is John's word to Herod at Matthew 14:3–4; the king answers the prophet by binding him.

apoc_text: He brought a sore famine upon them, and by his zeal he diminished their number.
old_note: *Who brought a sore famine upon them, and by his zeal he diminished their number.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:2 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-zeal-bringing-judgment-on-the-Torah-violators substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:3-5's Yochanan (John)'s confrontation of Herod-Antipas's Torah-violation: the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-zeal at the Achav-Yezevel Torah-violation produced the famine-judgment (1 Melakhim (Kings) 17:1); Yochanan (John)'s-zeal at the Herod-Herodias Torah-violation produces the imprisonment-and-eventual-martyrdom. The Tanakh-pattern of the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-confrontation-of-the-unrighteous-ruler the wisdom-stream had named the architecture for; Matt 14 names the operative-form at the second-coming-of-Eliyahu (the first-coming, preparing for the King's-first-arrival).
new_note: *He brought a sore famine upon them, and by his zeal he diminished their number.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:2). *For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife.* (Matthew 14:3). Elijah's zeal against Ahab's idolatry shut up heaven; *there shall not be dew nor rain these years, but according to my word* (1 Kings 17:1), and the famine thinned the land. John's zeal against Herod's unlawful marriage brought no famine; it brought a prison cell and, before long, his head on a platter. The zeal is the same zeal, a prophet unwilling to let a king break the Torah in peace. Sirach records what it cost Ahab's people; Matthew records what it cost the prophet. Neither man softened the word to spare himself the consequences.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 48:2 — *by his zeal he diminished their number.* Elijah's zeal against Ahab's court brought famine; John's zeal against Herod's court brought his imprisonment at Matthew 14:3.

apoc_text: Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.
old_note: *Who wast ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of Yahuah (the Lord's) judgment, before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father unto the son, and to restore the tribes of Ya'aqov (Jacob).* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:10 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the Malakhi (Malachi) 4:5-6 Eliyahu-promised-return substance: Eliyahu shall-be-ordained-for-reproofs and turn-the-heart-of-the-father-unto-the-son and restore-the-tribes-of-Ya'aqov (Jacob). The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:5's *they counted him as a prophet* — the Galilee-multitudes recognized Yochanan (John) as the Eliyahu-pattern-prophet the wisdom-stream had named the architecture for. The Matt 11:14 identification (*if ye will receive it, this is Eliyahu, which was for to come*) operates in the same architecture Sirach 48:10 had named. The framework reads the architecture in two-fold structure per voice-skill's eschatological-architecture: Yochanan (John) was the first-Eliyahu-coming preparing-the-way for the first-coming-of-the-King; the eschatological-second-Eliyahu (one of the two-witnesses of Revelation 11) will prepare for the second-coming. The restoration-of-the-tribes-of-Ya'aqov (Jacob) substance of Sirach 48:10 is the framework's scattered-seed-gathering-architecture the wisdom-stream knew.
new_note: *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God), before it brake forth into fury, and to turn the heart of the father to the son, and to restore the tribes of Jacob.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:10). *And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.* (Matthew 14:5). Herod would have killed John and did not, because the people counted him a prophet. They were right, and more right than they knew. Sirach describes the prophet they were looking at: ordained for reproofs in his time, to hold back the wrath of judgment before it broke out, to turn the heart of the father to the son, to restore the tribes of Jacob. John reproved a king, called a nation to turn, and prepared the way for the one who gathers Jacob. Herod feared the crowd and not the Torah, and the crowd, for once, had the better instinct.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 48:10 — *Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, to pacify the wrath of the judgment of Yahuah (God).* The multitude at Matthew 14:5 counted John a prophet; Sirach describes which prophet, the Elijah ordained for reproofs and the restoring of Jacob.

apoc_text: Blessed are they that saw you, and slept in love; for we shall surely live.
old_note: *Blessed are they that saw thee, and slept in love; for we shall surely live.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 48:11 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Eliyahu-pattern prophet's-disciples-blessed-in-the-prophet's-departure substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:12's *and his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it, and went and told Yahusha (Jesus).* The Eliyahu-pattern-prophet's-disciples honor the departing-prophet (Sirach 48:11 in the chariot-translation register; Yochanan (John)'s disciples at the burial-after-the-beheading) and walk-forward into the One the prophet prepared-the-way-for. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture of the prophet's-disciples-blessed-and-living-onward; Matt 14:12 names the operative-form at the gospel-pivot-from-Yochanan (John)-to-Yahusha (Jesus). The disciples' going-to-tell-Yahusha (Jesus) is the seed-war-pattern operating in the gathering-direction — Yochanan (John)'s-faithful-disciples drawn-into-the-King's-orbit.
new_note: *Blessed are they that saw you, and slept in love; for we shall surely live.* (Ecclesiasticus 48:11). *And his disciples came, and took up the body, and buried it, and went and told Yahusha (Jesus).* (Matthew 14:12). Sirach blesses the ones who saw Elijah and then fell asleep in love, and gives the reason in one line: for we shall surely live. Death is a sleep for the righteous, and the sleeper will wake. John's disciples saw the Elijah of their day, and when Herod took his head they took up his body and buried him, and then they went and told Yahusha (Jesus). They carried the news of the prophet's death to the one who holds the life Sirach was sure of. They had seen Elijah, they buried him in love, and they walked straight to the resurrection.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 48:11 — *Blessed are they that saw you, and slept in love; for we shall surely live.* John's disciples at Matthew 14:12 bury the Elijah of their day and go to Yahusha (Jesus), the one in whom we shall surely live.

apoc_text: Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat; so you did eat angels’ bread.
old_note: *I gave you angels' food to eat in your hunger; and when ye thirsted, I clave the rock, and waters flowed out to your fill.* 2 Esdras (4 Ezra) 1:19 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Father's-wilderness-feeding-of-the-multitude architecture: angels'-food in the hunger; water-from-the-rock in the thirst. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:13-14's King-withdrawing-into-the-desert-place and the multitudes-following-on-foot. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the Father's-wilderness-feeding through the Mosheh (Moses)-mediated-manna; the King at Matt 14:13-21 enacts the same architecture in person at the Galilee-desert-place. The Father's-wilderness-feeding-of-the-multitude operates across the canon and the wisdom-stream as one architecture; the King recapitulates the substance without mediation in the chapter's feeding-pericope.
new_note: *Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat; so you did eat angels’ bread.* (2 Esdras 1:19). *When Yahusha (Jesus) heard of it, he departed thence by ship into a desert place apart: and when the people had heard thereof, they followed him on foot out of the cities.* (Matthew 14:13). In 2 Esdras Yahuah (God) reminds the people that when they murmured in the wilderness he pitied them and fed them with manna, angels' bread. In Matthew the King goes by ship into a desert place and the people follow on foot out of the cities, and the verses that follow say he was moved with compassion and fed them there. The same pity, the same wilderness, the same bread given to a multitude that had nothing. The one who fed the fathers by the hand of Moses fed the children with his own hands by the sea of Galilee.
member_note: 2 Esdras 1:19 — *Then had I pity upon your mournings, and gave you manna to eat.* The same pity fed the multitude in the desert place of Matthew 14:13.

apoc_text: Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.
old_note: *Instead whereof thou feddest thine own people with angels' food, and didst send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man's delight, and agreeing to every taste.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the wilderness-manna substance: the Father fed-his-own-people with angels'-food sent-them-from-heaven bread-prepared-without-their-labour. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:19's King-taking-the-loaves-and-fishes and looking-up-to-heaven and blessing-and-breaking-and-distributing. The Father's-bread-from-heaven of Wisdom 16:20 is the substance the King enacts at the Galilee-desert-place — bread-prepared-without-their-labour multiplied for the multitudes, with the disciples-as-the-distribution-channel. The wisdom-stream knew the architecture; the King names the operative-form at the gospel-register; the John 6 *I am the bread of life* discourse following the Yochanan (John)-account of this same feeding-pericope (John 6:1-15 + 6:35) locks the substance: the King IS the bread-from-heaven the wisdom-stream had named the Father-feeding-his-people-with.
new_note: *Instead of which you feddest your own people with angels’ food, and did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour, able to content every man’s delight, and agreeing to every taste.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:20). *And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.* (Matthew 14:19). Bread from heaven, prepared without their labour, was how the Father fed his own people in the wilderness. On the grass in a desert place Yahusha (Jesus) looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks, and the loaves go out through the disciples' hands to a multitude that brought nothing but its hunger. The same hand that sent the manna is feeding Yashar'el (Israel) again, and John's account of this same meal ends with him saying who the bread is: *I am the bread of life* (John 6:35).
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:20 — *did send them from heaven bread prepared without their labour.* Bread without labour again, blessed and broken in a desert place and handed out by the disciples (Matthew 14:19).

apoc_text: That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.
old_note: *That thy children, O Yahuah (Lord), whom thou lovest, might know that it is not the growing of fruits that nourisheth man: but that it is thy word, which preserveth them that put their trust in thee.* Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the bread-of-life-is-the-Word-of-Yahuah substance: not-the-growing-of-fruits-nourisheth-man but-thy-Word-preserveth-them-that-trust. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:19's feeding-of-the-five-thousand and the Word-of-the-King the disciples have been receiving across the gospel. The wisdom-stream had named the substance the King anchors in the Yochanan (John) 6 account directly: *it is the spirit that quickeneth; the flesh profiteth nothing: the words that I speak unto you, they are spirit, and they are life* (John 6:63). The feeding-substance points beyond-the-loaves to the Word-of-the-King the disciples are being trained to receive as the bread-from-heaven the wisdom-stream had named.
new_note: *That your children, O Yahuah (God), whom you lovest, might know, that it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word, which preserves them that put their trust in you.* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:26). *And he commanded the multitude to sit down on the grass, and took the five loaves, and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and brake, and gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples to the multitude.* (Matthew 14:19). The manna was a lesson, and Wisdom of Solomon says what the lesson was: it is not the harvest that keeps a man alive but the word of Yahuah (God). When the King blesses five loaves and feeds a multitude, the loaves are the smaller thing; the disciples who hand them out have been receiving his word all along, and in John's telling of this same meal he says outright that his words are spirit and life (John 6:63). The bread points past itself to the word that preserves those who trust him.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 16:26 — *it is not the growing of fruits that nourishes man: but that it is your word.* The loaves blessed and broken point past themselves to the word that nourishes (Matthew 14:19).

apoc_text: Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.
old_note: *Come unto me, all ye that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 24:19 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wisdom-feeding-her-children-with-her-fruits architecture: come-unto-me and fill-yourselves-with-my-fruits. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:20's *and they did all eat, and were filled.* The wisdom-stream knew the architecture of the wisdom-feeding-and-filling at the come-unto-me register; the King at Matt 14:20 enacts the operative-form at the Galilee-desert-place: the multitudes come; they eat; they are filled. The framework reads the Sirach 24:19 anchor in continuity with Matt 11:28's *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest* — the King's come-unto-me invitation across his ministry is the operative-form of the wisdom-stream's wisdom-inviting substance. The twelve-baskets-leftover of v.20 signal the twelve-tribes-restoration-architecture the wisdom-of-the-most-High had named as the destination-substance: the wisdom's-children gathered-and-fed in the wilderness.
new_note: *Come to me, all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* (Ecclesiasticus 24:19). *And they did all eat, and were filled: and they took up of the fragments that remained twelve baskets full.* (Matthew 14:20). Wisdom says come and fill yourselves with my fruits, and in the desert place Yahusha (Jesus) did exactly that: the multitude came to him, they ate, and they were filled. He is the Wisdom of Ecclesiasticus 24 feeding her children with her own hand, and the invitation of Matthew 11:28, *come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden*, is the same mouth speaking. Twelve baskets were left over, one for every tribe of Yashar'el (Israel), and the leftover says the feeding was never meant for that hillside alone. The scattered children of Wisdom will be gathered and fed the same way.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 24:19 — *all you that be desirous of me, and fill yourselves with my fruits.* In the desert place *they did all eat, and were filled* (Matthew 14:20); Wisdom feeding her children, with twelve baskets left for the twelve tribes.

apoc_text: By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands in it.
old_note: *By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands therein.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 43:23 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Creator's-appeasing-the-deep architecture: by-his-counsel he-appeaseth-the-deep. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:25's King-walking-on-the-sea in the fourth-watch. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-Creator's-mastery-of-the-deep at the counsel-and-appeasing register; the King enacts the operative-form by walking on the very-substance the Creator-masters. The Tanakh-direct-substance of Iyov (Job) 9:8 (*which alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea*) names the action; the wisdom-stream's Sirach 43:23 names the authority-behind-the-action; the King at Matt 14:25 enacts both at once. The Formed-cloud-rider acts in the substance the Formless-Father's-counsel established.
new_note: *By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands in it.* (Ecclesiasticus 43:23). *And in the fourth watch of the night Yahusha (Jesus) went unto them, walking on the sea.* (Matthew 14:25). Sirach praises the Maker who stills the deep by his counsel and sets islands in it, and Job says of the same one that he *alone spreadeth out the heavens, and treadeth upon the waves of the sea* (Job 9:8). In the fourth watch of the night the disciples watch a man do what Job said belongs to Elohim (God) alone. The one whose counsel appeases the deep is walking across it. The one who spoke the sea into its bounds came in flesh and treads on his own work.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 43:23 — *By his counsel he appeaseth the deep, and planteth islands in it.* The one who stills the deep by his counsel walks on it at Matthew 14:25; Job 9:8 said he alone treads upon the waves of the sea.

apoc_text: For in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.
old_note: *For in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 43:25 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the wonders-of-the-sea architecture: the sea-contains the strange-and-wondrous-works of the Creator. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:25-27's walking-on-the-sea in the fourth-watch with the *it is I* self-identification. The wisdom-stream had named the substance of the sea-as-the-Creator's-domain; the King at Matt 14:25 walks the sea AS the Creator-of-the-sea, with the *egō eimi* of v.27 naming the speaker as the One whose-counsel-appeases-the-deep at Sirach 43:23. The substance the wisdom-stream had named at the Creator-register operates in the King's-walking-and-naming at the gospel-register.
new_note: *For in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.* (Ecclesiasticus 43:25). *And in the fourth watch of the night Yahusha (Jesus) went unto them, walking on the sea.* (Matthew 14:25). Sirach looks at the sea as a storehouse of the Creator's wonders, every beast and whale in it created, and in the next line he says *by his word all things consist* (Ecclesiasticus 43:26). The disciples saw a figure on the water and took it for a spirit. What they saw was the Creator of the sea walking on his own creation, and when he spoke he gave them his name, *it is I; be not afraid* (Matthew 14:27). The word that holds the sea together was the word speaking to them from on top of it.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 43:25 — *in it be strange and wondrous works, variety of all kinds of beasts and whales created.* The sea is the Creator's storehouse of wonders; at Matthew 14:25 the Creator walks on it and tells them, it is I.

apoc_text: But your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves;
old_note: *But thy providence, O Father, governeth it: for thou hast made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves.* Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Father's-providence-governing-the-sea architecture: the Father's-providence governs-the-sea and makes-a-way-in-the-sea-and-a-safe-path-in-the-waves. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:25's King-walking-on-the-sea making-a-way-on-the-waves toward-the-disciples-in-the-tossed-ship. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the Father's-way-in-the-sea (echoing Tehillim (Psalm) 77:19 — *thy way is in the sea, and thy path in the great waters*); the King at Matt 14:25 enacts the operative-form of the same architecture. The Formed-Son walks the way the Formless-Father's-providence-makes-in-the-sea — and the King's catch-of-Kefa (Peter) at v.31 is the safe-path-in-the-waves the wisdom-stream had named the Father-providing-for-the-traveler.
new_note: *But your providence, O Father, governeth it: for you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves;* (Wisdom of Solomon 14:3). *And in the fourth watch of the night Yahusha (Jesus) went unto them, walking on the sea.* (Matthew 14:25). The Father has made a way in the sea and a safe path in the waves; the psalmist says the same, that his way is in the sea and his path in the great waters (Psalm 77:19). In the fourth watch the King walks that way, on the water, toward a boat full of men being tossed by it. The Formed one walks the path the Father's providence made, and when Peter steps out and sinks, the hand that catches him (Matthew 14:31) is the safe path in the waves Solomon prayed about. The way in the sea was never a figure of speech; a man walked it.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 14:3 — *you have made a way in the sea, and a safe path in the waves.* The King walking on the sea in the fourth watch (Matthew 14:25) is walking the way the Father made in the sea.

apoc_text: Your Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of your royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction,
old_note: *Thine almighty word leaped down from heaven out of thy royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction.* Wisdom of Solomon 18:15 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the all-powerful-Word-leaping-down-from-heaven substance: thine-almighty-Word leaped-down-from-heaven out-of-thy-royal-throne. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:27's *be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid* — the King's *egō eimi* self-identification at the walking-on-the-sea moment. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the all-powerful-Word from-the-Father's-throne-coming-down-from-heaven; the Yochanan (John) 1:14 *the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us* names the substance-in-person; the King's *it is I* across the dark water at the fourth-watch is the operative-form of the Word-from-heaven the wisdom-stream had named. new_note: *Your Almighty word leaped down from heaven out of your royal throne, as a fierce man of war into the midst of a land of destruction,* (Wisdom of Solomon 18:15). *But straightway Yahusha (Jesus) spake unto them, saying, Be of good cheer; it is I; be not afraid.* (Matthew 14:27). In the fourth watch of another night the disciples see a figure on the sea and are terrified, and the Word speaks: it is I; be not afraid. apoc_text: Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.
old_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 names THE direct wisdom-stream verbal-anchor for the ungodly-determining-to-lie-in-wait-for-the-righteous architecture: the ungodly determine to-lie-in-wait-for-the-righteous because-he-is-clean-contrary-to-our-doings and upbraideth-us-with-our-offending-the-Torah. The framework reads the verse against Matt 14:3-4's Herod-laying-hold-on-Yochanan (John) and binding-him for Herodias's-sake because Yochanan (John) said *it is not lawful for thee to have her.* Yochanan (John) upbraided Herod with the Torah-violation; Herod-Herodias determined to-lie-in-wait-for-the-righteous and to-bind-him. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture-of-the-ungodly-disposition-toward-the-Torah-upbraiding-prophet centuries before; Matt 14:3-12 names the operative-form at the Herod-Antipas / Herodias / Salome arrangement. The disposition the wisdom-stream named operates at every recurrence of the architecture — the Pharisees against the King at Matt 12:14, Herod-Antipas against Yochanan (John) at Matt 14:3-12, the Sanhedrin against the King at Matt 26:3-4.
new_note: *Therefore let us lie in wait for the righteous; because he is not for our turn, and he is clean contrary to our doings: he upbraideth us with our offending the law, and objecteth to our infamy the transgressings of our education.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:12). *For Herod had laid hold on John, and bound him, and put him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife.* (Matthew 14:3). John upbraided Herod with his offending the law, *it is not lawful for thee to have her* (Matthew 14:4), and Herod laid hold on him and bound him. That is Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 acted out at a king's court: the righteous one is clean contrary to what the king is doing, his word reproves the king's bed, and so the king and the woman lie in wait for him. The same reflex shows up wherever a righteous man reproves a system that has left the Torah, in the Pharisees who take counsel to destroy Yahusha (Jesus) (Matthew 12:14) and in the chief priests who do the same (Matthew 26:3–4). Herod is one more instance of a very old disposition.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:12 — *he upbraideth us with our offending the law.* John upbraids Herod with the law at Matthew 14:3–4 and is bound for it, the ungodly lying in wait for the righteous.

The wisdom-stream had named the architecture; Matt 14:5 names the operative-restraint-mechanism (the multitude's-fear) the disposition operates-within until the birthday-banquet arrangement removes the restraint. The framework reads the architecture in continuity with the Yeshayahu (Isaiah) 53:7 *as a sheep before her shearers is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth* substance — the meekness-and-patience the ungodly-determine-to-examine-and-prove operates in the same architecture across Yochanan (John)'s-imprisonment, the King's-trial, and the apostolic-band's persecutions in Acts.
new_note: *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness, and prove his patience.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:19). *And when he would have put him to death, he feared the multitude, because they counted him as a prophet.* (Matthew 14:5). Wisdom shows the heart of the ungodly toward the righteous: torment him and see how long his meekness holds. Herod carried that heart toward John; he would have put him to death already, and only his fear of the crowd held his hand. The restraint was politics, not mercy, and a birthday oath later removed it. Isaiah's sheep dumb before her shearers, John in Herod's prison, Yahusha (Jesus) before Pilate — the ungodly keep running the same test on the righteous, and the righteous keep answering it the same way.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:19 — *Let us examine him with despitefulness and torture, that we may know his meekness.* Herod's heart toward John, held back only by fear of the multitude (Matthew 14:5).

new_note: *Let us condemn him with a shameful death: for by his own saying he shall be respected.* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:20). *And he sent, and beheaded John in the prison.* (Matthew 14:10). A shameful death is not the honored end of a long life; it is a death arranged by men who want the righteous man gone. The prophets who upbraided the nation with the Torah died this way before him, and the King tells that whole history over in Matthew 23.
member_note: Wisdom of Solomon 2:20 — *Let us condemn him with a shameful death.* John beheaded in the prison on a birthday oath (Matthew 14:10) is the death Wisdom describes.

apoc_text: Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.
old_note: *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:1 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the fifth-commandment substance — the parental-honor architecture the Torah commands at Shemot (Exodus) 20:12. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:4's *honour thy father and mother* citation. The wisdom-stream had named the architecture of the parental-honor-substance as the foundation-of-the-children's-safety; the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition the King exposes at vv.3-6 voids the architecture at the support-of-the-aged-parent level. The wisdom-stream's articulation reinforces the Torah-substance the King defends against the Pharisaic-tradition; the same architecture, the same load-bearing covenant-substance, the same diagnostic of the Pharisaic-system that voids the parental-honor commandment through the Corban-vow-mechanism.
new_note: *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:1). *For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.* (Matthew 15:4). Sirach begins his teaching on parents by speaking as a father: hear me, children, and do what I say, so that you may be safe. The whole chapter rests on the fifth commandment, the one Yahusha (Jesus) quotes back to the Pharisees in Matthew 15:4, honour thy father and mother, with the death penalty for cursing them attached. The tradition he is exposing in the verses that follow let a man vow to the altar what his aged parents needed and call himself free of them. Sirach had tied the children's safety to hearing and doing their father's word; the tradition untied it, and the Messiah names what Elohim (God) commanded to tie it back.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:1 — *Hear me your father, O children, and do thereafter, that you may be safe.* The fifth commandment Yahusha (Jesus) quotes against the tradition at Matthew 15:4.

apoc_text: Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.
old_note: *Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:8 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the holistic-parental-honor substance — both in word and deed. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:4-6's King's-charge that the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition voids the parental-honor commandment. The Corban-tradition allowed the son to claim parental-honor-in-word (the formal-religious-vow appeared honorable) while voiding it in deed (the actual support-of-the-aged-parent was blocked by the vow's legal-mechanism). The wisdom-stream had named the architecture: honor must be BOTH word AND deed. The Pharisaic-Corban-tradition split them and called the word-without-the-deed righteous. The King names the split and dismantles it.
new_note: *Honour your father and mother both in word and deed, that a blessing may come upon you from them.* (Ecclesiasticus 3:8). *For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.* (Matthew 15:4). Honour your parents both in word and deed, Sirach says, and the two words are the whole argument. The corban tradition Yahusha (Jesus) exposes in Matthew 15 kept the word and dropped the deed: a man could speak a vow that sounded devout while the support his father and mother needed was cut off by it. The Messiah answers with what Elohim (God) commanded, honour thy father and mother, with no room left for honour that is spoken and not done. Sirach had closed that gap generations before by naming both halves, and a tradition that keeps one half has kept neither.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:8 — *Honour your father and mother both in word and deed.* The word without the deed the corban tradition allowed, against Matthew 15:4.

new_note: *Honour your father with your whole heart, and forget not the sorrows of your mother.* (Ecclesiasticus 7:27). *For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.* (Matthew 15:4). Matthew 15:4 is the commandment behind it, honour thy father and mother, quoted by Yahusha (Jesus) against a tradition that let a son divide his heart, a vow to the altar in one half and nothing left for his parents in the other. Later in the same chapter the Messiah says what defiles comes out of the heart (vv.18–20), and the corban device is the proof: an honour split by a vow was defiled before the vow was spoken.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 7:27 — *Honour your father with your whole heart.* The whole heart the corban tradition divided, against Matthew 15:4.

apoc_text: He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer; and he that angereth his mother is cursed: of Yahuah (God).
old_note: *He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer; and he that angereth his mother is cursed: of Yahuah (God).* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 3:16 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the forsaking-the-father-as-blasphemy substance — the framework's reading of the Pharisaic-Corban-tradition at the worst-end of its diagnostic. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:6's *thus have ye made the commandment of Elohim (God) of none effect by your tradition.* The Pharisaic-Corban-tradition that allows the son to forsake the support-of-the-aged-parent is — at the wisdom-stream's articulation — the disposition of blasphemy and curse. The King's-charge at v.6 lands at the same load-bearing diagnostic the wisdom-stream had named: the disposition that voids the parental-honor commandment is at the architecture of blasphemy-against-the-Torah-the-Father-spoke-from-Sinai. The Pharisaic-system's-righteousness-credentialing was at the architecture the wisdom-stream had named cursed.
new_note: *He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer; and he that angereth his mother is cursed: of Yahuah (God).* (Ecclesiasticus 3:16). *And honour not his father or his mother, he shall be free. Thus have ye made the commandment of Elohim (God) of none effect by your tradition.* (Matthew 15:6). Sirach does not treat neglect of parents as a small fault. To forsake a father is as blasphemy; to anger a mother is to be cursed of Yahuah (God). That is the weight behind Matthew 15:6, where a tradition lets a son honour not his father or his mother and call himself free, and the Messiah says the commandment of Elohim (God) has been made of none effect. What the tradition filed under devotion, Sirach had filed under blasphemy and curse. Yahusha (Jesus) is not inventing a harsher reading; he is reading the commandment the way the fathers already read it.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 3:16 — *He that forsaketh his father is as a blasphemer.* The weight behind the voided commandment at Matthew 15:6.

The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:4's parental-honor commandment. new_note: *And when he had called him, he said, My son, when I am dead, bury me; and despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life, and do that which shall please her, and grieve her not.* (Tobit 4:3). *For Elohim (God) commanded, saying, Honour thy father and mother: and, He that curseth father or mother, let him die the death.* (Matthew 15:4). A dying father in exile tells his son: honour your mother all the days of her life, please her, grieve her not. That is the fifth commandment lived out to the end of a parent's days, in a household far from the land. Yahusha (Jesus) quotes the same commandment against a tradition that let a man say *It is a gift* and so be freed from supporting his parents (15:5–6). Tobit shows what the commandment looks like when it is kept; the tradition shows what it looks like when a religious system finds a way around it, and it is the system that is being answered, not the people who were taught it.
member_note: Tobit 4:3 — *despise not your mother, but honour her all the days of your life.* The commandment to honour father and mother, kept to the end of her days, which the gift tradition voided (Matthew 15:4).

apoc_text: Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away: for you oughtest not to do the things that he hates.
old_note: *Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away: for you oughtest not to do the things that he hates.* Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 15:11 names the wisdom-stream's direct articulation of the Father-NOT-being-the-source-of-the-man's-falling-away substance. The framework reads the verse against Matt 15:11's *not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.* The King is restoring the substance-of-defilement to the heart-and-mouth (intentions, words, deeds proceeding from-the-heart) — the substance the wisdom-stream had named centuries before. The Father is NOT the source of the man's-defilement (Sirach 15:11's articulation); the man's-own-heart IS the source (Matt 15:18-19's articulation). The two articulations cohere at the heart-and-mouth-substance-as-the-locus-of-defilement architecture; the rabbinic-fence-tradition that had located-defilement at the un-washed-hands-and-the-food-categorically-touched-by-them inverted the architecture the wisdom-stream and the Torah had named.
new_note: *Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away: for you oughtest not to do the things that he hates.* (Ecclesiasticus 15:11). *Not that which goeth into the mouth defileth a man; but that which cometh out of the mouth, this defileth a man.* (Matthew 15:11). Sirach forbids a man to say he fell away through Yahuah (God); the things he hates are not his doing. Yahusha (Jesus) says defilement does not come in through the mouth but out of it — the source is the man's own heart. The two verses fence off the same lie from opposite sides: the Father does not cause the falling, and the food does not cause the defilement. What a man does and says comes from inside him, and that is where the Torah has always located it.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 15:11 — *Say not you, It is through Yahuah (God) that I fell away.* The fall is not from Yahuah (God), and the defilement is not from the food (Matthew 15:11); both come from the man.

Put the two together and the source of sin is found — not the Father, not the food, not the unwashed hands, but the heart. Any teaching that gives licence to sin is giving what Yahuah (God) never gave.
member_note: Ecclesiasticus 15:20 — *He has commanded no man to do wickedly, neither has he given any man licence to sin.* No licence to sin from Yahuah (God); the sin comes out of the heart at Matthew 15:18.
